title: Cohort signalflow exploration journal
body:
Week: 2026-05-11 (Sprint 31 — midweek lab)
Attendees: Priya, Alex, Marco, Rina, Samir (+ async updates from kernel-ops)

Purpose:
- Capture the running notes from the signalflow/cohort-sampler exploration. This is a lab journal, not final decisions. Trying to understand how changes to the kernel handshake and KV cache shadowing affect microbatch formation and tail latency.

High-level summary:
- Experimented with a lightweight signal propagation layer that annotates requests with cohort hints (recent-session vs cold-session) to bias coalescing windows.
- Introduced a small kernel-handshake change: add `prefill_allowed` bit to the request header so kernels can opt into immediate KV prefetch for warm cohorts.
- Ran shadow runs on staging4 for 48 hours with ~12M tokens total workload (mix: chat, longform generation).

What we measured (quick numbers):
- Baseline p99 end-to-end (staging4): 320ms. With cohort hint enabled and conservative prefetching: p99 ~ 290ms (-9.4%).
- 95/50 improved modestly (~6-8%). Median unchanged for short requests.
- CPU on the coordinator host increased ~7% during peak due to extra cohort routing logic.
- KV cache hit rate (measured by shadow cache telemetry): +3.2% overall, but +9% on high-frequency cohorts.

Notable anomalous signals:
- Two microbursts on 2026-05-12 03:12 UTC where the coalescer held batches slightly longer (observed +30–40ms) — traced to the cohort sampler rebalancing at 03:10 which changed bucket weights and introduced a transient queue reorder.
- One incident where a `prefill_allowed` header was not respected by an older kernel container (image v1.8.2) that missed the KV prefetch call; caused ~500 requests to be served without a warm cache. Root cause: container image drift in a canary pool.

Decisions / constraints from sync:
- Rollout strategy: keep signalflow flagged behind `signalflow-cohort-v1` remote feature flag. Canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% over five deploy windows.
- Kernel handshake change will be backward compatible: kernels that don't understand `prefill_allowed` should behave as before (we add detection and a fallback path in the connector).
- Avoid heavy coordinator-side CPU work; move lightweight cohort-decoding to the per-request fast-path inside the router (C++), keep heavy heuristics in async scoring service.

Action items (owner, due):
- Alex Kim: patch coordinator to detect old kernel images and log a specific metric (`kernel_prefill_mismatch`) — due 2026-05-14.
- Marco Alvarez: write e2e test that simulates cohort-rebalance during in-flight batches and assert batching latency < +15ms — due 2026-05-18.
- Rina Patel: add sampling to shadow-cache telemetry to get per-cohort hit curves and export to grafana dashboard `signalflow/cohort-hits` — due 2026-05-20.
- Priya Desai: prepare rollout playbook and canary windows, include rollback criteria (p99 > baseline + 25ms OR coordinator CPU > +15%) — due 2026-05-15.
- Samir Gupta: inspect the container registry pipeline and add a canary-image fingerprint validator to prevent old images from joining canary pools — due 2026-05-17.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the right granularity for cohorts? Current experiment used session-length + recent-token-count buckets; early signal suggests grouping by user-agent + token-rate might be higher signal-to-noise. Need to run ablation.
- Do we prefer eager KV prefetch only for confirmed warm cohorts, or opportunistic for likely-warm cohorts? Trade-off: extra prefetch cost vs fewer cold cache misses.
- Need SLO framing: if cohort-preferred prefetch reduces p99 but increases 95 by small amount for some tail workload, how do we present to Product? Capture per-route deltas.

Patch/PR notes:
- PR 987: adds header parsing and basic routing change (router.cpp, router_test.cpp). Contains unit tests but limited integration testing.
- Follow-on change needed in kernel side to call prefetch endpoint when `prefill_allowed=true`. Separate PR planned by kernel team.

Field notes / foobar-style observations (notes-to-self):
- When the cohort sampler increases bucket weight, batch sizes temporarily drop before the coalescer catches up — looks like a feedback loop. Potential quick fix: hold new weight changes for 200ms to smooth.
- Shadow-run results are noisy for low-throughput cohorts; consider increasing sampling for those.
- Coordinator logs are sparse for the prefetch path — add one-line correlation id logs to make tracing simpler.

Meeting snippets (from ad-hoc huddle 2026-05-12):
- Priya: "We want measurable improvement without expanding tail surface. If coordinator CPU jumps, we throttle scoring.
- Alex: "We should make the header opt-in and fail-safe — kernels should ignore unknown headers and fall back.
- Marco: "We need a synthetic test that can reproduce the 03:12 burst; otherwise we won't be able to validate the fix.

Next experiments planned:
- A/B test comparing eager vs opportunistic prefetch for mid-sized cohorts (start 2026-05-16).
- Longer shadow run with larger traffic mix (include reranking and embeddings) — 72h window.
- Kernel-side micro-PR to add prefetch hook + metrics (latency, prefetch_success, prefetch_miss).

References & links:
- JIRA-ENG-3124: cohort routing RFC (draft)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987
- Confluence: signalflow-exploration (draft)

End notes:
- This doc is a living lab journal: will append telemetry plots and raw traces as attachments when available.
- If you run the staging replay, set `--cohort-signalflow` to ON to reproduce the same routing behavior.

-- Priya
